Definition 1 (Grid-locked block-sequential sampler; position-only policy) . A grid-locked block-sequential sampler is any acquisition that (a) samples a static field along the fast axis at positions locked to the absolute grid { m ​ Δ ​ y } \{m\Delta y\} , (b) acquires in blocks of a fixed count n c n_{c} , one per traversal, and (c) re-initializes between blocks with a nonzero latency per ( 2 ). There is a grid-locked block-sequential sampler, a position-only policy, and an adversary { τ i } \{\tau_{i}\} under which L1 holds for every block while L2 fails. The pitch Δ ​ y \Delta y enters only through L1 (the spacing), so shrinking it cannot repair the origin disagreement, which is set by { τ i } \{\tau_{i}\} . ∎ Theorem 1 makes “position fidelity is not phase fidelity” precise: the two guarantees are logically independent, and only the first is delivered by grid-locked triggering. Section IV sharpens “fails” into an impossibility, identifies the minimal primitive that restores L2, and gives the tight timing tolerance; Section V asks when a broken { k i } \{k_{i}\} is recoverable after the fact. VII Discussion What the results say together. Grid-locked triggering fixes where samples land (L1) but not which crossing becomes each block’s origin (L2): the two are logically independent (Theorem 1 ), and no position-only policy can close the gap under adversarial re-initialization (Theorem 3 ). What does close it is a single, quantifiable resource. An origin-coupled primitive P ⋆ P^{\star} that arms before the origin and pins record 0 0 to it removes the offset exactly (Theorem 4 ); an imperfect reference still succeeds, but only if it resolves the phase to within half a grid cell at the fastest speed, δ < Δ ​ y / ( 2 ​ v max ) \delta<\Delta y/(2v_{\max}) (Theorem 5 ).

The same half-cell constant reappears when the offset is recovered after the fact—from timestamps (Corollary 2 ) or from image texture above the Robinson–Milanfar limit (Proposition 2 )—so Section V-D presents it as a single half-cell condition shared by the three channels. Design rule: pay the half-cell margin in one channel. Pinning a block’s phase costs one resolved half-cell, and that cost must be paid by exactly one of three channels—at the trigger (a synchronization reference, prevention), in the metadata (a sub-interval timestamp, exact recovery), or in the image texture (a shift estimate resolving half a column, statistical recovery). This is a design heuristic within the studied setting , not a universal conservation law. Quantitatively, a fixed trigger-to-capture gap δ \delta displaces the origin by Φ = δ ​ v / Δ ​ y \Phi=\delta v/\Delta y cells, so the half-cell condition Φ < 1 / 2 \Phi<1/2 is a speed–pitch fidelity envelope v < Δ ​ y 2 ​ δ ⟺ Δ y > 2 δ v , v<\frac{\Delta y}{2\delta}\qquad\Longleftrightarrow\qquad\Delta y>2\delta v, (7) a maximum faithful speed for a target pitch; with the calibrated δ ≈ 110 ​ μ \delta\approx 110\,\mu s (Section VI ) the 5 ​ μ 5\,\mu m/ 390 390 mm/s capture sits far outside it, consistent with the large measured offset, so the operating rule is to keep δ ​ v < Δ ​ y / 2 \delta v<\Delta y/2 . A pipeline that pays the margin in no channel leaves the phase unrecoverable—and Proposition 3 shows the texture-free and periodic bands are exactly where the texture option is unavailable, which is why the certificate (Section V-E ) abstains there rather than fabricate. The counterintuitive cadence lesson. Tightening the block count to exactly the number of imaged columns—the natural way to remove the surplus that hides the offset—does not help; it induces a subharmonic capture cadence under any re-initialization latency (Corollary 1 ), degrading throughput to one row per bidirectional cycle in the worst case.

Surplus re-hides the offset; only the origin-coupled handshake fixes both the offset and the cadence. This is a concrete warning for triggered-DAQ raster design. Instantiation on a real system. Section VI exhibits the phenomenon on a position-triggered laser-ultrasound C-scanner (on-grid spacing with nonzero per-block offsets, the catastrophic straddle, the subharmonic cadence). The logged configuration is a position-only acquisition policy, and it shows a nonzero per-block offset on almost every block—an empirical instance of the failure Theorem 3 predicts for position-only policies. The offset is recoverable off-line where the image is identifiable, by an image-based registration estimator with an identifiability certificate (the image channel of Section V ). A rate-matched, logged capture that decomposes the per-block L2 offset from the intra-block L1 warp on the same region—the measurement flagged in Section VI-A —is what would turn Fig. 1 into a fully quantitative L2 claim. Scope and limitations. The theory is confined to inter-block phase (L2). We bracket the continuous intra-block warp (an L1 effect, dominant at submicron pitch on the deployed system, Supplementary Table S5) as a separate problem; entangling the two obscures both, and the decomposition is precisely what lets us report each cleanly. The recovery certificate controls risk only where it does not abstain , and assumes exchangeability of the calibration set (recalibrate under distribution shift); it does not identify the unrecoverable set exactly. The average-case autoregressive model (Section V-F ) is motivated by an observed offset autocorrelation measured in a different, large-offset regime and is used only as a modelling choice; fitting it at the operating point is a measurement still to be made. Generality of the sampler class.

The object of study—a grid-locked block-sequential sampler (Definition 1 )—covers scanning electron and transmission electron microscopy with flyback, atomic-force and scanning-probe line scanning with re-trace, push-broom and line-scan cameras, optical-coherence B-scan stacking, and ultrasonic/photoacoustic raster C-scanning. No result depends on the instrument; each needs only count-locked capture, absolute-grid triggering, and a nonzero re-initialization latency. The rolling-shutter analogy is instructive by contrast: rolling shutter is a continuous warp at known row times, whereas the corruption here is an unknown, discrete relabeling of the column origin for a static scene under a known trajectory—invisible to row-time motion models. Structural versus statistical. Section VI-C draws the boundary that the certificate exposes: abstention soundness is a structural property, distribution-free and carrying across modalities, whereas how completely the certificate abstains and how tightly it controls kept-region risk are statistical and modality-specific. A single cross-modal invariant does not hold, and we make no universal-law claim. Certified abstention and generative hallucination. The core principle—a system should decline rather than fabricate when its input is provably uninformative—connects to a broader concern: hallucination in generative models, where image restorers and language models alike synthesize confident but unsupported output [ 1 ] . Our certificate is an existence proof that, where an identifiability structure is computable, fabrication can be provably prevented rather than merely reduced. The mechanism here derives from the likelihood surface of a well-posed estimation problem; generative-model confabulation lacks an equivalent computable identifiability surface, so the mechanism does not transfer directly.

We therefore frame this not as a solution to hallucination but as evidence that certified abstention under provable unidentifiability is achievable in at least one broad class of problems [ 5 , 32 ] , and as an invitation to identify computable identifiability structures in others. Grid-locked triggering fixes where samples land (L1) but not which crossing becomes each block’s origin (L2): the two are logically independent (Theorem 1 ), and no position-only policy can close the gap under adversarial re-initialization (Theorem 3 ). What does close it is a single, quantifiable resource. An origin-coupled primitive P ⋆ P^{\star} that arms before the origin and pins record 0 0 to it removes the offset exactly (Theorem 4 ); an imperfect reference still succeeds, but only if it resolves the phase to within half a grid cell at the fastest speed, δ < Δ ​ y / ( 2 ​ v max ) \delta<\Delta y/(2v_{\max}) (Theorem 5 ). The same half-cell constant reappears when the offset is recovered after the fact—from timestamps (Corollary 2 ) or from image texture above the Robinson–Milanfar limit (Proposition 2 )—so Section V-D presents it as a single half-cell condition shared by the three channels. We bracket the continuous intra-block warp (an L1 effect, dominant at submicron pitch on the deployed system, Supplementary Table S5) as a separate problem; entangling the two obscures both, and the decomposition is precisely what lets us report each cleanly. The average-case autoregressive model (Section V-F ) is motivated by an observed offset autocorrelation measured in a different, large-offset regime and is used only as a modelling choice; fitting it at the operating point is a measurement still to be made. VIII Conclusion Absolute-position triggering does not, by itself, produce a spatially faithful pixel array: it guarantees intra-block position (L1) but not inter-block phase (L2), and the two are independent (Theorem 1 ). No position-only policy can restore L2 (Theorem 3 ); an origin-coupled synchronization primitive is necessary and sufficient to guarantee L2 at acquisition within the count-locked policy class of Definition 1 (Theorem 4 ), and an imperfect reference suffices iff it resolves half a grid cell at the fastest speed (Theorem 5 ). When phase fidelity is broken, the offsets are exactly recoverable from metadata, conditionally recoverable from image texture above an explicit detectability threshold, and provably ambiguous in texture-free and periodic regions, where a distribution-free certificate abstains rather than hallucinate. A single half-cell condition governs prevention and both recovery channels in this setting. On a deployed laser-ultrasound C-scanner we measure the predicted failure directly—a rigid 17.3 17.3 -column bidirectional index offset—and the speed–pitch envelope v < Δ ​ y / ( 2 ​ δ ) v<\Delta y/(2\delta) turns the half-cell condition into an operating rule: keep δ ​ v < Δ ​ y / 2 \delta v<\Delta y/2 , or supply a sub-half-cell reference. The contract and its separation give designers of triggered raster inspection systems a precise target—resolve the phase cell somewhere in the pipeline—and a clear account of where, provably, it cannot be recovered at all.
